exercises.name: Bodyweight squat
exercises.cue: Sit back, knees track over toes, stand tall.
howToDoIt: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, letting them travel out over your toes. Chest stays up.
Go as low as you can with your heels flat and your lower back neutral, then drive through the floor to stand tall.
exercises.shouldFeel: Work through the thighs and glutes. Your heels stay down the whole time.
exercises.commonMistake: Knees collapsing inward, or heels lifting near the bottom. Either one means you have gone past the depth you currently own.
exercises.easier: Sit down to a chair or bench and stand back up. Same movement, less depth.

exercises.name: Split squat
exercises.cue: Short stance, drop the back knee, keep the front heel down.
howToDoIt: Step one foot forward into a short stance, feet about hip-width apart side to side.
Lower straight down until the back knee is just off the floor, front heel flat.
Drive through the front foot to stand. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
exercises.shouldFeel: The front thigh and glute working, with a stretch across the front of the back hip.
exercises.commonMistake: A stance so long it becomes a lunge, or the front heel lifting as you descend.
exercises.easier: Hold a wall or doorframe for balance, and stop the descent higher.

exercises.name: Reverse lunge
exercises.cue: Step back, both knees near 90 degrees, push through the front foot.
howToDoIt: Stand tall, then step one foot straight back.
Lower until both knees are near 90 degrees, torso upright.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, then alternate sides.
exercises.shouldFeel: The front leg doing the work. The back leg is mostly there for balance.
exercises.commonMistake: Leaning the chest out over the front knee, or letting that knee drift inward.
exercises.easier: Hold a wall for balance, or take a shorter step back.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.cue: Ribs down, squeeze glutes at the top, don't overarch.
howToDoIt: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and about hip-width apart.
Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body makes a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower with control.
exercises.shouldFeel: Glutes and hamstrings. You should not feel this in your lower back.
exercises.commonMistake: Arching the low back to get higher. The height comes from the hips finishing, not the spine bending.

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
exercises.cue: One foot planted, hips square, pause at the top.
howToDoIt: Lie on your back with one foot planted close to your glutes, the other leg lifted.
Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips, keeping both hip bones level.
Pause at the top, then lower with control. Finish all reps on one side before switching.
exercises.shouldFeel: The glute of the planted leg doing the work.
exercises.commonMistake: Letting the lifted side drop so the hips twist, or pushing through the toes instead of the heel.
exercises.easier: Do a two-leg glute bridge, or rest the lifted foot lightly on the floor for support.

exercises.name: Calf raise
exercises.cue: Slow lower, full range, equal work left and right.
howToDoIt: Stand tall with your feet hip-width and your weight through the balls of the feet.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes.
Lower slowly, all the way down, before starting the next rep.
exercises.shouldFeel: The calves through a long range. The slow lower is where most of the work is.
exercises.commonMistake: Bouncing at the bottom and cutting the range short at both ends.
exercises.easier: Hold a wall for balance and keep both feet on the floor.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.cue: Hips stacked, body in a straight line, breathe.
howToDoIt: Lie on your side with your forearm under your shoulder and your feet stacked.
Lift your hips until your body makes one straight line from head to heels.
Hold, breathing normally, then repeat on the other side.
exercises.shouldFeel: The side of your waist nearest the floor, and the shoulder holding you up.
exercises.commonMistake: Hips sagging toward the floor, or the chest rolling forward so you are no longer on your side.
exercises.easier: Bend your knees and hold from the knees rather than the feet.

exercises.name: Dead bug
exercises.cue: Low back stays heavy on the floor as opposite arm and leg move.
howToDoIt: Lie on your back with your arms straight up and your knees over your hips, bent at 90 degrees.
Press your low back into the floor and keep it there for every rep.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor, then return and alternate.
exercises.shouldFeel: A deep brace across the abdominals, hardest when the arm and leg reach furthest.
exercises.commonMistake: Letting the low back arch off the floor as the leg lowers. That is the moment the exercise stops working.
exercises.easier: Move the legs only, or lower them a shorter distance.

exercises.name: Bird dog
exercises.cue: Reach long, keep hips level, pause, switch.
howToDoIt: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso.
Pause, return with control, then switch sides.
exercises.shouldFeel: The back of the shoulder, the glute of the reaching leg, and a brace through the middle holding you still.
exercises.commonMistake: Letting the hips tip as the leg lifts, or lifting the leg above hip height and arching the back.
exercises.easier: Move one limb at a time -- arm only, then leg only.

exercises.name: Push-up
exercises.cue: Body plank-stiff, elbows ~45 degrees, chest to a fist off the floor.
howToDoIt: Hands under your shoulders, body plank-stiff from head to heels.
Lower until your chest is about a fist's height off the floor, elbows tracking back at roughly 45 degrees.
Push the floor away and return to the top without letting your hips sag.
exercises.shouldFeel: Chest, shoulders and triceps working, midsection braced throughout.
exercises.commonMistake: Hips sagging toward the floor, or elbows flaring straight out to the sides.
exercises.easier: Put your hands on a bench, a step, or a wall. The more upright you are, the easier it gets.

exercises.name: Band row
exercises.cue: Pull elbows back, squeeze shoulder blades, don't shrug.
howToDoIt: Anchor the band at chest height and hold an end in each hand with your arms straight.
Pull your elbows back past your ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Return slowly, keeping tension in the band the whole way.
exercises.shouldFeel: The mid-back between the shoulder blades, with the shoulders staying down.
exercises.commonMistake: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears, or pulling with the hands so the elbows flare wide.
exercises.easier: Step closer to the anchor, or use a lighter band.

exercises.name: Dumbbell row
exercises.cue: Hinge, back flat, pull the weight to the hip.
howToDoIt: Hinge at the hips with a flat back, one hand supported on a bench or your thigh.
Let the weight hang, then pull it to your hip with the elbow close to your body.
Lower under control. Finish the side before switching.
exercises.shouldFeel: The lat down the side of the back, and the mid-back at the top of the pull.
exercises.commonMistake: Twisting the torso to lift the weight higher, or letting the back round as it lowers.
exercises.easier: Go lighter and slow the lowering down.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
exercises.cue: Hold the weight at the chest, sit between the heels.
howToDoIt: Hold one weight against your chest with both hands, elbows tucked in.
Sit down between your heels, keeping your chest tall and your heels flat.
Drive through the floor to stand.
exercises.shouldFeel: Thighs and glutes, with the upper back working to keep the chest up.
exercises.commonMistake: The chest falling forward as you descend, which turns it into a hinge rather than a squat.
exercises.easier: Go lighter, or squat down to a box and stand back up.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.cue: Soft knees, push hips back, feel the hamstrings, stand tall.
howToDoIt: Stand tall holding the weight in front of your thighs, knees softly bent.
Push your hips straight back and let the weight slide down your legs, back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings, then drive your hips forward to stand tall.
exercises.shouldFeel: A clear stretch down the back of the thighs on the way down, glutes at the top.
exercises.commonMistake: Rounding the lower back, or turning it into a squat. The knee angle barely changes through the whole rep.
exercises.easier: Go lighter, or with no weight at all, and shorten the range — stop halfway down.

exercises.name: Step-up
exercises.cue: Whole foot on the box, drive up, control the lower.
howToDoIt: Place one whole foot on the box -- the heel must be on it, not hanging off the edge.
Drive through that foot to stand up on the box, without pushing off the trailing foot.
Lower slowly under control. Finish the side, then switch.
exercises.shouldFeel: The stepping leg's thigh and glute. The other leg should feel like a passenger.
exercises.commonMistake: Pushing off the back foot to get up, which lets the working leg do far less than it looks.

exercises.name: Hip thrust
exercises.cue: Upper back on the bench, chin tucked, squeeze at lockout.
howToDoIt: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, feet flat and about hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel with the floor.
Squeeze the glutes at the top with your chin tucked, then lower with control.
exercises.shouldFeel: The glutes, hard, at the top of every rep.
exercises.commonMistake: Arching the low back and lifting the ribs at the top instead of finishing with the glutes.
exercises.easier: Do the same movement from the floor, without the bench.

exercises.name: Pull-up or hang hold
exercises.cue: Shoulders down and back. Use a hang if pull-ups are not ready.
howToDoIt: Hang from the bar with your hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Pull your shoulders down and back first, then drive your elbows toward your ribs until your chin passes the bar.
Lower all the way to a full hang under control.
exercises.shouldFeel: Lats and upper back. The arms help, but should not be doing all of it.
exercises.commonMistake: Kicking the legs to generate swing, or stopping short of a full hang between reps.
exercises.easier: Hold a dead hang for time, or jump to the top and lower yourself slowly.

exercises.name: Swiss ball crunch
exercises.cue: Hips stay still, curl the ribs toward the pelvis.
howToDoIt: Sit on the ball and walk your feet out until your low back is supported on it.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis, lifting your shoulders a short way.
Lower back over the ball with control.
exercises.shouldFeel: The abdominals through a longer range than a floor crunch, because the ball lets you start extended.
exercises.commonMistake: Pulling on the back of your neck, or moving at the hips instead of curling the spine.
exercises.easier: Extend back over the ball a shorter way, and cross your arms on your chest.

exercises.name: Farmer carry
exercises.cue: Tall posture, ribs stacked, walk slow and even.
howToDoIt: Pick up a weight in each hand and stand tall with your ribs stacked over your hips.
Walk at a steady, even pace with your shoulders down and the weights quiet.
Keep walking for the full time, then set the weights down under control.
exercises.shouldFeel: Grip, shoulders, and a constant brace through the whole midsection.
exercises.commonMistake: Leaning back to counter the load, or letting the weights swing so the torso twists with them.
exercises.easier: Go lighter, or carry one weight at a time and swap hands halfway.

exercises.name: Front plank
exercises.cue: Squeeze glutes, push the floor away, breathe.
howToDoIt: Set your forearms on the floor under your shoulders, elbows bent about 90 degrees.
Step your feet back until your body makes one straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes, push the floor away with your forearms, and breathe normally for the whole hold.
exercises.shouldFeel: A deep brace across the entire midsection. Shoulders and glutes should be working too.
exercises.commonMistake: Hips drifting up into a pike, or sagging toward the floor. Both take the work off the abdominals.
exercises.easier: Drop to your knees, or set your forearms on a bench so your body sits at an angle.
